Count what comes with the purchase

By v/hNovember 20, 2026Document

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

Count what the owner has to buy besides the device.

Imagine a utility that works with household containers. If it only accepts a container sold by its maker, the owner may have to replace items that still do their job.

Our starting requirement would be to work with suitable items people already own. A local agent could help handle differences in shape or placement, but it cannot remove a physical requirement for a seal, a material or a secure fit.

Sometimes a matched part is necessary. Then its purpose, purchase price, replacement needs and future availability belong in the design decision.

A useful development check: list every required purchase beside the device. For each one, ask what makes it necessary and whether the same result could be achieved with something the owner already has.

Our first utility is in development. The container example is illustrative. These are design requirements to establish, not compatibility claims.
